result.target_topic: Estimates of uninsured deposits at year-end 2024 and 2023
result.target_summary: At December 31, 2024, the Corporation's total estimated uninsured U.S. and non-U.S. deposits were $646.2 billion and $124.9 billion, respectively, compared to $606.8 billion and $116.6 billion at December 31, 2023. These estimates exclude $16.9 billion and $14.8 billion of collateral on derivative contracts netted against derivative assets at December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively, and reflect regulatory report disclosures adjusted to exclude accrued interest and intercompany balances.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both disclosures report the estimated amounts of uninsured U.S. and non-U.S. deposits at year-end, the insurance limits, and adjustments for derivative collateral netting. The 2023 disclosure (D224) covers the 2023 year-end data and the 2024 disclosure (D224) covers the 2024 year-end data with comparable methodology and structure.

comparisons.peer_topic: Specific Deposit Programs and Insurance Coverage
comparisons.peer_summary: Consumer deposits include Marcus and Apple Card customers, while FDIC-insured deposits were $234.54 billion as of December 2024 and non-U.S. insured deposits were $25.98 billion as of the same date.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies report specific figures for FDIC-insured and non-U.S. insured deposits, allowing for an implicit comparison of the insured portion of their deposit bases, though neither explicitly states a total 'uninsured' aggregate like BAC or JPM. GS reported FDIC-insured deposits of $234.54 billion and non-U.S. insured deposits of $25.98 billion as of December 2024. BAC, in contrast, focuses on the uninsured estimate, stating total estimated uninsured U.S. and non-U.S. deposits were $646.2 billion and $124.9 billion respectively, noting that U.S. deposits are insured up to $250,000 per depositor.

sentences.text: The FDIC insures the Corporation's U.S. deposits up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank for each account ownership category, and various country-specific funds insure non-U.S. deposits up to specified limits.
At December 31, 2024, the Corporation's deposits totaled $1.97 trillion, of which total estimated uninsured U.S. and non-U.S. deposits were $646.2 billion and $124.9 billion.
• Deposits insured by the FDIC were $234.54 billion as of December 2024 and $221.52 billion as of December 2023.
• Deposits insured by non-U.S. insurance programs were $25.98 billion as of December 2024 and $26.00 billion as of December 2023.

comparisons.peer_topic: Uninsured deposit estimates and insurance coverage
comparisons.peer_summary: At December 31, 2024, estimated uninsured deposits were $1,414.0 billion, primarily wholesale operating deposits, with coverage varying by country such as FDIC insurance in the U.S., while all non-U.S. time deposits are deemed uninsured.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM disclose total estimated uninsured deposits at year-end 2024, showing a similar upward trend. BAC reported $646.2 billion in U.S. and $124.9 billion in non-U.S. uninsured deposits (totaling ~$771.1 billion) at Dec 31, 2024, compared to $606.8 billion and $116.6 billion in 2023. JPM reported total estimated uninsured deposits of $1,414.0 billion at Dec 31, 2024, up from $1,347.8 billion in 2023. JPM specifies that its uninsured deposits are primarily wholesale operating deposits and that non-U.S. time deposits are deemed uninsured, whereas BAC explicitly excludes derivative collateral and accrued interest from its estimates.

sentences.text: At December 31, 2024, the Corporation's deposits totaled $1.97 trillion, of which total estimated uninsured U.S. and non-U.S. deposits were $646.2 billion and $124.9 billion.
At December 31, 2023, the Corporation's deposits totaled $1.92 trillion, of which total estimated uninsured U.S. and non-U.S. deposits were $606.8 billion and $116.6 billion.
At December 31, 2024 and 2023(a), the Firmwide estimated uninsured deposits were $1,414.0 billion and $1,347.8 billion, respectively, primarily reflecting wholesale operating deposits.
For purposes of this presentation, all non-U.S. time deposits are deemed to be uninsured.
